whatItDoes: Turn one scene description into a short stitched video. An LLM breaks the scene into a style guide and an ordered shot list, generates each keyframe, animates it into a clip, and joins the clips. Run it with no input and it shoots the built-in sample as one real, cheap shot.
longDescription:
Give it one scene description and it produces a short, multi-shot video with a consistent look across shots. An LLM (`models.run`) writes a style guide and breaks the scene into an ordered shot list, then image and video generation turn that plan into finished clips.

The work runs as a durable pipeline, and both the keyframes and the clips render one at a time: each image or video job runs in the background and the agent run pauses until a webhook says it's ready, then moves to the next. Running each stage in sequence keeps a paused step always waiting before its job can finish. Once every clip is collected, a merge job stitches them into a single video (a one-shot run skips the merge — one clip is already a finished video).

Run it with no input and it shoots the built-in sample scene as a single shot, so the zero-setup run is real and cheap rather than a dry run. Supply your own `scene` and a larger `numShots` for a fuller multi-shot video, or set `dryRun` to stop right after planning and see the shot list without generating anything.

This is the priciest template in the gallery once you go past one shot. A full run pays for one LLM call, one image per shot, one image-to-video clip per shot, and (for more than one shot) the merge job — so start with a small `numShots`.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

Run it with no input and it shoots the built-in sample scene as one real, cheap shot — a single keyframe, one clip, no merge job. Pass your own `scene` for a fuller multi-shot video (`numShots`, default 3, max 6): it bills the LLM plan, one image per shot, one image-to-video clip per shot, and a merge job once you're past one shot. Set `dryRun: true` to stop after planning and see the shot list without paying for any images or video. It renders one keyframe and one clip at a time and picks each up on its own; you don't send any signal. It defaults to Kling 2.1 Pro for the video; pass a cheaper `model` (a Wan or Seedance image-to-video id) to trade quality for cost.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "dryRun": true }` to trace the whole graph for free, or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.

input.scene: a paper boat drifting down a rain-soaked city gutter at night

output.bible: Moody neo-noir night scene: a small white paper boat on dark rain-slicked asphalt, amber streetlight reflections, shallow depth of field, 35mm anamorphic look, cool blue shadows.

shots.image_prompt: Moody neo-noir night scene... Close-up of the paper boat entering a flooded gutter, raindrops rippling the surface.
shots.motion_prompt: The paper boat; drifts into frame on the current; slow push-in; 6s; amber streetlight; anamorphic neo-noir.
